questions.q:
Statement I: An interpreter reports an error as soon as it reaches the faulty statement during execution.
Statement II: Compiled programs generally execute faster than interpreted programs.
Which is correct?
questions.exp: Interpreters translate and run line by line, stopping at the first error; compiled machine code runs faster as no translation is needed at run time.

questions.q: How does calloc(5, sizeof(int)) differ from malloc(5 * sizeof(int))?
options: calloc allocates memory on the stack
Memory from calloc need not be freed
calloc initialises the allocated memory to zero
questions.exp: Both allocate heap memory that must be released with free(). calloc takes two arguments (count, size) and zero-fills the block; malloc leaves it uninitialised.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following algorithm?
a = 48, b = 18
while b != 0
  t = b
  b = a mod b
  a = t
print a
questions.exp: This is Euclid's algorithm: gcd(48, 18) = gcd(18, 12) = gcd(12, 6) = gcd(6, 0) = 6.
Assigning a double to an int truncates the fractional part, giving 3.

questions.q: Which of the following translates the whole source program into object code before execution begins?
questions.exp: A compiler translates the entire program in one go; an interpreter translates and executes statement by statement.

questions.q: Recursive function calls in C are managed internally using which data structure?
questions.exp: Each call pushes an activation record on the call stack, which is popped on return.

questions.q: Which function is best suited to read a whole line of text (including spaces) from the keyboard safely into a character array?
questions.exp: fgets reads up to a newline including spaces and limits the characters read to the buffer size.

questions.q: Which storage class specifier is used to refer to a global variable that is defined in another source file?
questions.exp: extern declares a variable whose definition (storage) lies elsewhere, typically in another file.

questions.q: Wrapping data and the functions that operate on it into a single unit (class) is called
questions.exp: Encapsulation binds data and methods together and restricts direct access to the data.

questions.q: The macro EOF defined in stdio.h is an integer constant that usually has the value
questions.exp: EOF is a negative integer constant, conventionally -1, returned by functions like fgetc at end of file.

questions.q: The call strcmp("Zebra", "apple") returns
questions.exp: strcmp compares ASCII values: 'Z' (90) is less than 'a' (97), so the result is negative.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): In C, an array name cannot be assigned a new value (for example a = b; is illegal for arrays).
Reason (R): The array name evaluates to the address of its first element, which is fixed and not a modifiable lvalue.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.exp: The array name is a non-modifiable lvalue representing a fixed base address, which is why assignment to it is illegal.

questions.q: The memory allocated to a union variable in C is equal to
options: the sum of the sizes of all its members
the size of its smallest member
the size of its largest member (with possible padding)
the product of the sizes of its members
questions.exp: All members of a union share the same memory, so the space needed is that of the largest member.

questions.q:
What is the value of x after the statement?
int x = 2 + 3 * 4 % 5;
questions.exp: *, % have higher precedence than + and associate left to right: 3*4 = 12, 12%5 = 2, then 2 + 2 = 4.

questions.q: Which of the following operators has the lowest precedence in C?
questions.exp: The comma operator has the lowest precedence of all C operators.

questions.q: An assembler is a translator that converts
questions.exp: An assembler translates mnemonics of assembly language into machine code.

questions.q:
Match the file function with its purpose:
1. fopen   2. fclose   3. fputc   4. fseek
P. Move the file position indicator   Q. Open a file   R. Close a file   S. Write one character
questions.exp: fopen opens, fclose closes, fputc writes a character and fseek repositions the file pointer.

questions.q: What does malloc() return when it cannot allocate the requested memory?
questions.exp: malloc returns a NULL pointer on failure, so the result should always be checked before use.
Values are printed on the way down (3 2 1) and again while the calls return (1 2 3).

questions.q: Which of the following can hold the value of only one of its members at any given time?
questions.exp: Members of a union overlap in memory, so only one member's value is meaningful at a time.

questions.q: Which storage class requests that a variable be kept in a CPU register, and does not allow its address to be taken?
questions.exp: The register storage class hints that the variable should be stored in a register, hence the & operator cannot be applied to it.

questions.q:

questions.q: Which phase of a compiler is executed first?
questions.exp: Lexical analysis converts the source text into tokens and precedes syntax analysis, semantic analysis and code generation.

questions.q: Which preprocessor directive is used to remove the definition of a previously defined macro?
questions.exp: #undef NAME cancels a macro definition made with #define.

questions.q: Which fopen() mode opens a file for both reading and writing and fails if the file does not exist?
questions.exp: "r+" requires an existing file and allows read and write; "w+" truncates/creates and "a+" creates if absent.

questions.q: Class and object are the central concepts of which programming paradigm?
questions.exp: Object-oriented programming organises software around objects created from classes.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a desirable characteristic of an algorithm?
options: Having zero or more inputs and at least one output
questions.exp: Every step of an algorithm must be precisely defined; ambiguity is not allowed.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes #include "myfile.h" from #include <myfile.h>?
options: The first form is used only for standard library headers
The second form searches the current directory before the standard directories
The first form searches the current directory first and then the standard directories
There is no difference between the two forms

questions.q: In a flowchart, which symbol is used to represent a decision (yes/no branching)?
questions.exp: The diamond (rhombus) symbol is used for decision making; the rectangle is a process, parallelogram is input/output and oval is start/stop.

questions.q: When an array is passed as an argument to a function in C, what is actually passed?
options: A complete copy of the array
Only the size of the array
The address of the first element
questions.exp: The array name decays to a pointer to its first element, so the function works on the original array.

questions.q: Which C library function returns a non-zero value when the end of a file has been reached?
questions.exp: feof(fp) tests the end-of-file indicator of the stream.

questions.q: Which of the following is a derived data type in C?
questions.exp: int, char and float are fundamental types; arrays, pointers, structures and unions are derived types.

questions.q:
Statement I: A C function can directly return more than one value using a single return statement.
Statement II: A function can change variables of the caller if it receives their addresses.
Which is correct?
questions.exp: A return statement returns a single value, but pointer parameters let a function modify the caller's variables.

questions.q: Given struct s { int a; float b; }; which statement correctly declares a variable v of this type in C?
questions.exp: In C the keyword struct must be used with the tag name (unless typedef is used): struct s v;

questions.q: Macro substitution (#define) is carried out by which of the following?
questions.exp: The preprocessor expands macros and includes header files before actual compilation begins.

questions.q: Which construct is discouraged in structured programming because it makes control flow hard to follow?
questions.exp: Structured programming relies on sequence, selection and iteration and avoids unrestricted jumps such as goto.

questions.q: Which declaration makes fp a pointer to a function that takes two int arguments and returns int?
questions.exp: The parentheses in (*fp) bind the * to fp, so fp is a pointer to a function. Without them, int *fp(int, int) declares a function returning int*.

questions.q: Which of the following is a valid identifier in C?
questions.exp: An identifier must start with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, digits and underscores; 'int' is a keyword.

questions.q:
Match the language with its main paradigm:
1. C   2. Java   3. Prolog   4. Haskell
P. Procedural   Q. Object-oriented   R. Logic   S. Functional
questions.exp: C is procedural, Java is object-oriented, Prolog is a logic language and Haskell is purely functional.
